items.text: Claude GitHub App installed on ck5o4/multifamily with write access - cloud push unblocked
items.why: FIXED 2026-08-17 by Anthony. Root cause was subtler than 'a missing scope': the Claude app was AUTHORIZED on ck5o4 but INSTALLED only on the flux-brain-hq org, never on the personal account that owns multifamily. Authorization is what let cloud sessions read; installation is what grants repo Contents:write, so every push 403'd while every read succeeded - exactly the observed asymmetry. Installed via github.com/apps/claude/installations/new -> ck5o4 -> Only select repositories -> multifamily. Verified at installation 154488689: 'Read and write access to ... code' and 'Selected 1 repository: ck5o4/multifamily'. Scoped to that one repo deliberately. NOTE: the post-install redirect lands on claude.ai/admin-settings/... which shows 'You don't have access to organization settings' on a personal plan - that dead end is cosmetic, not a failure. Confirm on the next scheduled sweep that it pushes instead of emailing a recovery patch.

items.text: St. Bernard Parish is IN the buy box - resolved by modelling, not by rule
items.why: RESOLVED 2026-08-17 by running the same 12-unit building through three parishes instead of arguing from millage. Price that clears 13%: Baker $528K (equity $146,520), Gretna $397K (equity $110,168), Chalmette $388K (equity $107,670). Chalmette vs Gretna is a $9,000 / 2.3% difference - noise. St. Bernard's heavier millage is NOT what moves the number. The $140K / 26.5% gap vs Baker is the METRO WIND INSURANCE ($3,000/unit vs $2,000), which hits Jefferson and Orleans identically. Conclusion: excluding St. Bernard while buying Gretna is incoherent - same deal, 2.3% apart. All three fit inside $300K capital comfortably, so capital is not the binding constraint on metro deals; the insurance quote is. Chalmette listing itself is Zone X shaded, NOT SFHA, so no lender-required flood policy - but that is post-Katrina levee protection, not natural safety, so price a voluntary policy.
